headline: Hawkish Fed talk gives the dollar its best week since September; yen pinned near 160
summary: The dollar index rose about 0.2% to near 103.4, its highest since April 2025 and up about 1% on the week, as Fed officials kept a December hike fully priced and 10-year yields rose to about 5.15%, shrugging off a softer 0.3% rise in October PPI. The Aussie and euro fell most as AI stocks slid again, while the Taiwan dollar and rupiah firmed on equity inflows and Bank Indonesia support, and Tokyo's warnings held the yen just under 160.
drivers: Fed hike pricing holds despite a softer PPI

Producer prices rose 0.3% in October against 0.4% expected, but annual PPI hit 6.5%, a four-year high, and a key core gauge rose 0.5%. A 25bp hike in December stays about 90% priced, with a 12–15% chance of 50bp; two-year yields ended the week up about 35bp at 4.87%, their biggest weekly jump since 2024.
AI selloff hits the Aussie and euro

The Nasdaq fell 0.9% as Nvidia slid again after its CEO's exit, and copper hit its lowest since July. The Aussie dropped about 0.5% to near 0.6774, a 10-month low, and the euro slipped to about 1.1023, its weakest since April 2025.
Officials guard the yen and the rupiah

USD/JPY briefly topped 160 for the first time since September, to about 160.19, before Finance Minister Katayama's warning about one-sided moves knocked it back to about 159.7. Bank Indonesia's NDF and spot support lifted the rupiah 0.2% to 18,206 from Thursday's record low.
view: Still bullish for the next 1–2 weeks: the Fed is set to hike in December and markets already price a follow-up in January, while the RBA and BoC look done and the ECB is near the end, so I keep backing the dollar against the Aussie, loonie and euro. I fade it only against the yen near 160, where Tokyo is on watch and the BoJ may hike in December. A DXY close back below 102.5, soft US data or a dovish turn from Fed speakers would turn me neutral.
ideas: Hold the long from 1.4080–1.4100 as yield spreads punish the loonie; for 1.4450, stop raised to 1.4200.
Hold the sale filled at 160.00–160.20 as Tokyo guards 160; for 157.50, stop 161.00.
Hold the sale from 0.6900–0.6920 as the RBA stands pat and AI stocks slide; target extended to 0.6700, stop cut to 0.6820.
review: The dollar calls gained again: the EUR/USD short is about 150 pips in favour, AUD/USD about 135 and USD/CAD about 175, so I trail stops and extend the euro and Aussie targets; the USD/JPY sale filled at 160.0–160.2 and is about 40 pips up. The ringgit closed above my 4.085 cap so turns long, the rupiah long is flat, and all other ranges held.

eurusd.note: Down about 0.25% to near 1.1028 after 1.1023, the lowest since April 2025; the short is about 150 pips in favour.
eurusd.why: The dollar did the moving. Fed officials kept talking up hikes, so a softer 0.3% PPI barely dented December pricing, and 10-year yields rose to about 5.15%. The euro's own news was mildly supportive, with Bundesbank chief Nagel calling another ECB hike highly probable and a December move about 72% priced, but that is far less than the Fed is set to deliver.
eurusd.outlook: I hold the short, extend the target to 1.0950 and cut the stop to 1.1075 to lock in most of the gain: the Fed is still outpacing an ECB near the end of its cycle. A close back above 1.1075 would say the dollar's rally has stalled.
eurusd.watch: Fed and ECB speakers, euro zone flash PMIs (late Nov), US PCE (late Nov), French bond spreads.

view.call: Short from 1.1170–1.1190; Fed outpaces a late-cycle ECB.

gbpusd.note: Down about 0.2% to near 1.3211, a fourth daily loss, inside my 1.3150–1.3350 range.
gbpusd.why: The dollar did the moving. Higher US yields and fresh hawkish Fed talk lifted the greenback, while the pound had no UK data of its own on Friday. BoE hike pricing, with a second rise to 4.25% on Dec 17 seen as likely, kept sterling firmer than the euro and Aussie, so the drop was modest.
gbpusd.outlook: I keep the 1.3150–1.3350 range: BoE hike bets support the pound, but the Fed caps rallies. A close below 1.3150, the October low, would turn me bearish; firm UK wages and CPI next week could lift it toward the top.
gbpusd.watch: UK jobs (Nov 17), UK CPI (Nov 18), BoE speakers, Fed speakers.

view.call: 1.3150–1.3350; BoE hike bets vs firm Fed.

audusd.note: Down about 0.5% to near 0.6774, a 10-month low; the sale is about 135 pips in favour.
audusd.why: Both sides moved. The dollar firmed on Fed hike bets and higher US yields, while the Aussie, the market's main risk proxy, fell as the Nasdaq dropped 0.9% on a second day of AI selling and copper hit its lowest since July. At home the RBA is seen on hold, so the rate gap keeps widening in the dollar's favour.
audusd.outlook: I hold the sale, extend the target to 0.6700 and cut the stop to 0.6820 to protect the gain: the RBA is done, the Fed is hiking and AI stocks are wobbling. A close above 0.6820 would end the call.
audusd.watch: Nvidia results (Nov 17), Australia jobs (Nov 19), monthly CPI (Nov 25), China data, US-China summit.

view.call: Sale from 0.6900–0.6920; RBA done, Fed hiking.

usdjpy.note: Down about 0.1% to near 159.69 after a spike to about 160.19; my sale at 160.00–160.30 filled.
usdjpy.why: The two sides pulled against each other. The Fed repricing pushed the pair above 160 for the first time since September, but Finance Minister Katayama called the moves one-sided and rapid and said Tokyo would work with the US Treasury, which knocked it back. Rising bets on a BoJ hike in December also limit the yen's losses.
usdjpy.outlook: I hold the sale for 157.50 with a stop at 161.00: Tokyo spent about ¥15.4tn defending the yen this summer and is warning again, and the BoJ may hike in December. A close above 161 would show officials are standing aside.
usdjpy.watch: Tokyo comments near 160, Japan Q3 GDP (Nov 16), BoJ speakers, US yields.

view.call: Sale filled 160.00–160.20; Tokyo guards 160, BoJ may hike.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.4% to near 0.8382 after touching about 0.8397, just under my 0.8400 range top.
usdchf.why: The dollar did the moving. US 10-year yields rose to about 5.15% while the SNB holds at 0%, so the rate gap again favoured the dollar, ending two weeks of franc gains. The AI-stock selloff gave the franc little haven support because the broader US market fell only 0.4% and the Dow edged higher.
usdchf.outlook: I keep the 0.8250–0.8400 range with an upward tilt: the rate gap favours the dollar, but the October high and SNB intervention risk cap it near 0.84. A close above 0.8400 would open a long toward 0.8500.
usdchf.watch: Fed speakers, SNB comments, equity sentiment, Swiss inflation (early Dec).

usdcad.note: Up about 0.1% to near 1.4270; the buy is about 175 pips in favour, off Thursday's 1.4331 peak.
usdcad.why: The rate gap did the moving. Canada's two-year yield has fallen about 20bp further below the US since early November, to a 147bp gap, after a third straight month of job losses and hot US inflation; Scotiabank called the spread move punishing for the loonie. Oil was flat, with Brent near $95.8, so it gave no offset.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the buy for 1.4450 and raise the stop to 1.4200, under this week's lows, to lock in a gain: the Fed is still ahead of the BoC. A hot Canada CPI that revives BoC hike bets would be the main risk.
usdcad.watch: Canada CPI (Nov 17), BoC speakers, oil and US-Iran headlines, Fed speakers.

view.call: Long from 1.4080–1.4100; wide US-Canada yield gap.

usdcnh.note: Little changed near 6.675 offshore as the PBOC set another far-weaker-than-expected fixing.
usdcnh.why: Beijing did the moving again. The PBOC set the midpoint at 6.7152, about 396 pips weaker than the market estimate of 6.6756, its fourth big weak gap in a row, and raises banks' FX reserve ratio to 6% from 4% on Nov 15 to slow the yuan's rally. Exporters converting dollar holdings kept the yuan firm against a stronger dollar.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep the 6.64–6.70 range: the PBOC leans against gains while exporters sell dollars on rallies. A close above 6.70 would show Beijing wants a weaker yuan; below 6.64 would show it is letting the rally run.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15), China activity data, US-China summit.

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC slows the yuan, exporters sell USD.

usdhkd.note: Steady near 7.8455, about 45 pips from the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved the pair. US two-year yields held near 4.87% after their biggest weekly jump since 2024, keeping the gap over HIBOR wide and the carry trade into US dollars attractive. That holds the Hong Kong dollar near the weak end of its band, close to its weakest this year.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: the carry gap keeps it near 7.85, and only a jump in HIBOR or HKMA buying at 7.85 would pull it lower.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA operations at 7.85, HIBOR, Fed speakers.

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Up about 0.1% to near 1.2881, inside my 1.2780–1.2920 range.
usdsgd.why: The dollar did the moving. Hawkish Fed talk and higher US yields kept the dollar firm across Asia, and the second day of AI selling weighed on the region's tech-heavy markets. The Singapore dollar still held up better than most, gaining slightly against the ringgit, because the MAS keeps it on a gently rising path against its basket.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2780–1.2920 range: the MAS band limits losses, but a Fed set to hike keeps the pair firm. A close above 1.2920 would open a long toward 1.3000.
usdsgd.watch: Singapore final Q3 GDP and non-oil exports, Fed speakers, Asian tech-stock flows.

usdkrw.note: Won fell 6.0 to 1,336.7 in Seoul as the Kospi lost 1%; offshore about 1,337.
usdkrw.why: Both sides moved. The Kospi opened up 2% but closed down 0.98% as worries over Nvidia's leadership returned, and foreigners turned net sellers of about ₩550bn. Thursday's 3% jump in Brent to near $96 also hurt the won, as Korea imports nearly all its oil, while the stronger dollar added pressure.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep the 1,330–1,365 range: exporter selling and recent inflows favour the won, but a Fed set to hike and fragile chip stocks limit gains. A Seoul close below 1,325 would open 1,315; above 1,365 would revive the long.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows, Nvidia results (Nov 17), oil and US-Iran headlines, Fed speakers.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar rose 5.1 cents to 32.838 in Taipei, trading 32.827–32.920; turnover US$2.21bn.
usdtwd.why: Equity inflows did the moving. Foreign investors bought a net NT$28.8bn of Taiwan shares, ending an 11-day selling streak, as the Taiex rose 1.35% on gains in MediaTek and other custom-chip names; local suppliers said Nvidia's CEO change would have limited impact. That outweighed the stronger dollar and kept the pair well below 33.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep the 32.60–33.05 range: officials defend 33 and foreign buying has resumed, but the AI-stock wobble and Fed hikes limit the Taiwan dollar's gains. A close above 33.05 would show the defence has failed; below 32.60 would open 32.40.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, Nvidia results (Nov 17), central bank action, Fed speakers.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit eased to 4.0845/0890 at the 6pm KL close from 4.0765/0805, above my 4.085 cap.
usdmyr.why: The dollar did the moving. Futures fully price a Fed hike in December with some chance of 50bp, and that lifted the dollar across Asia. The ringgit rose against the euro and pound and fell only slightly against regional peers, so the weakness was about the dollar rather than Malaysia.
usdmyr.outlook: The close above 4.085 turns me long toward 4.12 with a stop at 4.065: Fed hike bets outweigh Bank Negara's steady 2.75% rate for now. A close back below 4.065 would say the break has failed.
usdmyr.watch: Bank Negara comments, regional chip stocks, oil, Fed speakers.

view.call: Long 4.080–4.090; break of 4.085 on Fed hike bets.

usdphp.note: Peso slipped 2 centavos to 63.72 at the BAP close after hitting 63.94 intraday.
usdphp.why: The dollar did the moving. Sustained dollar demand and Fed hike bets pushed the peso toward its record low near 64.17 intraday, with volume rising, before it recovered most of the loss into the close. Steady oil, with Brent flat near $95.8, gave it some relief after Thursday's jump.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 63.30–64.20 range with the record low as the cap: holiday remittances help, but oil and the Fed weigh. A close above 64.20 would mark a new record and open 64.80.
usdphp.watch: Oil and US-Iran headlines, BSP comments, Fed speakers, BSP decision (Dec 17).

usdidr.note: Rupiah rose 33 points to 18,206 from Thursday's record low; JISDOR 18,218.
usdidr.why: Bank Indonesia did the moving. Dealers said BI stepped in through offshore NDFs, domestic forwards, spot and bond buying, and a budget update showing revenue growing faster than spending helped sentiment. The rupiah still lost 0.65% on the week as Fed bets, MSCI index cuts and political uncertainty weighed.
usdidr.outlook: I hold the long toward 18,500 with a stop at 18,080: MSCI outflows and the Fed outweigh BI's smoothing, though BI's firmer hand means the climb will be slow. A close back below 18,080 would show BI has regained control.
usdidr.watch: Bank Indonesia operations and decision (Nov 18–19), MSCI changes (effective Nov 30), politics, Fed speakers.

view.call: Long 18,200–18,250; MSCI outflows and Fed vs BI.

usdinr.note: Rupee fell 7 paise to 94.19, trading 94.05–94.28, inside my range.
usdinr.why: The dollar did the moving. Hot US inflation, higher Treasury yields and hawkish Fed talk lifted the dollar, and weak local stocks added pressure. Recent heavy foreign buying of Indian shares and lower oil than earlier in the autumn limited the damage, so the rupee stayed near its strongest levels since April.
usdinr.outlook: I keep the 93.50–94.50 range: inflows and RBI hike bets after 6.09% CPI help the rupee, but dollar buying by state banks and the Fed cap it. A close above 94.50 would open 95.
usdinr.watch: RBI decision (Dec 4), oil and US-Iran headlines, foreign equity flows, Fed speakers.

view.call: 93.50–94.50; inflows and RBI bets vs Fed.

eurjpy.note: Down about 0.35% to near 176.1, mid-range, as the euro fell and the yen held.
eurjpy.why: Both sides nudged it lower. The euro lost about 0.25% to the dollar as US yields rose, and the yen firmed slightly after Katayama's warning pushed USD/JPY back from 160. Talk of a BoJ hike in December added a little yen support, but the cross stayed inside its range.
eurjpy.outlook: I keep the 175.5–178.0 range: intervention risk and BoJ hike bets cap the yen's losses, while ECB hikes limit the euro's. A close below 175.5 would open 174.
eurjpy.watch: Tokyo comments, Japan Q3 GDP (Nov 16), ECB speakers, French spreads.

view.call: 175.5–178.0; ECB hikes vs yen intervention risk.

cnhjpy.note: Little changed near 23.92, in the upper half of my 23.6–24.2 range.
cnhjpy.why: Neither side moved much. The yuan held near 6.675 per dollar on exporter selling and the PBOC's weak fixings, and the yen held near 159.7 as Tokyo warned against one-sided moves. With both currencies anchored by officials, the cross stayed close to Thursday's level.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.6–24.2 range: the yuan is held steady, so the cross follows USD/JPY, which Tokyo is likely to cap near 160. A close above 24.2 would show intervention is not coming.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15), Tokyo comments near 160, Japan Q3 GDP (Nov 16).

view.call: 23.6–24.2; yen near Tokyo's line, yuan held.

watch: Next: the PBOC's FX reserve hike (Nov 15), Japan Q3 GDP (Nov 16), Canada CPI, UK jobs and Nvidia results (Nov 17), UK CPI (Nov 18), Bank Indonesia (Nov 18–19), Australia jobs (Nov 19), then the RBI (Dec 4), Fed (Dec 8–9) and BoE (Dec 17), plus Tokyo's 160 line and Taiwan's defence of 33.
